common_name: Flavor Queen Pluot (Sweet Yellow-Skinned Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; needs a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer nearby. Flavor Queen is a Zaiger Genetics pluot, an interspecific hybrid combining plum and apricot parentage weighted toward plum, producing golden-yellow skinned fruit with sweet, richly flavored, apricot-tinged yellow flesh that ripens in mid to late summer. Like other pluot varieties, it delivers intensely concentrated, complex sweetness that many growers find surpasses either parent species on its own, a hallmark of the entire pluot breeding program. Thin fruit if the tree sets a heavy crop, and harvest once fruit yields to gentle pressure and reaches full color, since pluots do not continue ripening much once picked, unlike some other stone fruit.

common_name: Dapple Fire Pluot (Dramatic Dappled Red-Green Skin, Red-Fleshed)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; needs a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer nearby. Dapple Fire is a Zaiger Genetics pluot notable for its striking appearance, with dark green skin splashed and streaked with fiery red dapples that intensify as the fruit ripens, opening to reveal firm, deep red flesh with a rich, sweet-tart flavor and good, dense texture. The visual drama of the skin pattern makes it a favorite at farmers markets and among home orchardists who enjoy growing something visually distinctive alongside more conventionally colored stone fruit. Thin fruit if the tree sets heavily, and harvest once fruit yields to gentle pressure, since the dappled skin can make judging ripeness by color alone trickier than with solid-colored varieties.

common_name: Splash Pluot (Yellow Skin with Red Splash Pattern)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; needs a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer nearby. Splash is a Zaiger Genetics pluot with pale yellow skin marked by irregular red splashes and streaks, giving each fruit a slightly different, hand-painted appearance, and it produces sweet, juicy, richly flavored flesh typical of the best pluot selections. The tree is a reliable producer within the pluot family, and the fruit's bright, cheerful coloring along with its excellent eating quality has made it a popular choice among specialty fruit growers and farmers market vendors. Thin fruit if the tree sets heavily to concentrate flavor and size, and harvest once fruit yields to gentle pressure and the splash pattern has fully developed.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible plum or pluot pollinizer nearby. Flavor Heart is a Zaiger Genetics pluot notable for its distinctive elongated, heart-like fruit shape, with dark red to nearly maroon skin covering rich, sweet, deeply flavored red-tinged flesh characteristic of the best pluot varieties. The unusual fruit shape sets it apart visually from the more typically round or oval pluots, making it a conversation piece as well as a good-eating specialty stone fruit for home orchards. Thin fruit if the tree sets a heavy crop, and harvest once fruit yields to gentle pressure and has fully colored, since pluots generally do not continue to ripen significantly after picking.

Honey Punch is a Zaiger Genetics 'nectaplum,' an interspecific hybrid combining nectarine and plum genetics, producing smooth-skinned, deep red fruit with dense, richly flavored red-tinged flesh that carries the smooth skin and juiciness of nectarine along with the depth of flavor plum breeding contributes. As with other Zaiger interspecific stone fruit hybrids, the combination produces a genuinely distinctive eating experience different from either parent species grown alone, with concentrated sweetness and complex flavor prized by specialty fruit growers. Thin fruit if the tree sets a heavy crop, and harvest once fruit yields to gentle pressure and fully colors for the best flavor.
